newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr awaits Tuesday, and then the fireworks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr awaits Tuesday, and then the fireworks.

text.p: Dollar trading should keep dealers on edge through Tuesday afternoon with three upcoming events having the potential to decide the U.S. currency's trend, analysts said on Friday.
"You'll know everything you need to know by Wednesday, Japan's trade numbers, the Bundesbank's repo rate and the Fed," said MCM CurrencyWatch senior analyst Keven Harris.

Japan's trade data for July will be released on Sunday night. The Bundesbank announces its repo rate policy on Tuesday, just hours before the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets U.S. benchmark rates.
Any of these three events could jumpstart a fresh dollar rally -- or spell trouble, analysts said.
Based on the market reaction, dollar/mark could move to either end of a 1.8050 to 1.8500 band. Meanwhile, dollar/yen may either probe strong support at 115.55 or try for the August 6 high at 119.58.

"The worry to a return to variable repo rates in Germany has to be there. The Bundesbank does not want to go out with its reputation in complete shamble," Harris said of the diminished role that the Bundesbank will be left with in 1999, once the euro and the European central bank are launched.

"The pivot area right now is around the 1.8250-mark level. Below that, the dollar will stay on the defensive, and may move down to 1.8050. Above 1.8250, we'll run into resistance at 1.85," predicted Mike Malpede, senior analyst at Refco.
In late Friday afternoon trading, dollar/mark was quoted at 1.8200/10 and dollar/yen at 117.56/61.
"On Monday, there is a good chance we'll see a reversal in dollar/yen," added Malpede who saw 119.50 as key resistance.
Once again, the dollar's fate is likely to be influenced by mark/yen, a cross that steadily crept up this week from the 62.00 to the 64.50 area.

"Mark/yen has the potential to climb above the 65.00 level, maybe to 66.00," added Malpede who noted that cross reflected "the Bundesbank sending signals they are going to tighten" and "less concern that Japan will defend the yen."
Like Harris, Malpede said Japan's trade data, and the interest rate decision by the Bundesbank and the Fed "will generate some expectable volatility."
Analysts also said support at 1.4925 Swiss francs could be pivotal for a dollar/Europe rally or retreat. A sterling/mark retreat to 2.9125 would be a dollar/mark negative.
